chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from al-Yamani, who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) say: 'How truly amazing, the utmost amazement, is for one who works for the abode of perishing [the world] yet abandons the abode of the Hereafter.'

key_terms.الدَّارُ: The abode or dwelling place, used here to refer to realms of existence.
key_terms.الْآخِرَةُ: The Hereafter, the eternal realm after death.
key_terms.الْفَنَاءُ: Perishing, transience, or impermanence, referring to the worldly life.
key_terms.عَجَبًا: An expression of wonder or astonishment.

ai.seo_question: What does Ali ibn al-Husayn say about working for the world versus the Hereafter?
ai.summary: Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) expresses astonishment at those who exert effort for the transient worldly life while neglecting the eternal abode of the Hereafter. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, serves as a core ethical exhortation in Shia tradition to prioritize the afterlife over temporary worldly gains, framing *zuhd* not as abandonment of the world but as correct orientation of effort. The 'astonishment' highlights the irrationality of investing finite labor in a decaying domain while ignoring the permanent reward.
